key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even with deep defect levels, recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganization and energy release, limiting SRH losses.
engineering_relevance: t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics because realistic point-defect concentrations are unlikely to explain its observed efficiency limits.
method: First-principles defect calculations over a large, chemically diverse point-defect dataset
Quantified defect-assisted SRH recombination rates for both radiative and nonradiative channels
Analyzed dependence on defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping
evidence_signal: The study reports that nonradiative multiphonon emission is suppressed and radiative defect-assisted capture is too small to explain device losses, even across many deep gap states.
watch_item: The conclusions address point-defect SRH only, so other loss mechanisms, microstructure effects, or processing-induced defects may still limit real devices.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
